headline: Flat quarter, steep guidance cut on soft U.S. pet demand
summary_short: Zoetis's Q2 2026 revenue was flat y/y at $2,468M (-0.2% y/y, +9.1% q/q) as an 11% drop in U.S. companion-animal sales offset livestock and international growth; diluted EPS rose 1.2% y/y to $1.65, but the company cut full-year revenue guidance to $9.120-$9.320B from $9.680-$9.960B.
summary_long: Revenue held flat at $2,468M as an 11% decline in U.S. companion-animal sales — driven by dermatology and Simparica Trio price sensitivity, generic pressure on Cerenia and Convenia, and lower Librela sales — offset 23% U.S. livestock growth and 8% international growth led by parasiticides and diagnostics. Net income fell 4.8% y/y to $691M ($1.65 diluted EPS, +1.2% y/y); adjusted diluted EPS was $1.87. Zoetis cut full-year 2026 guidance sharply: revenue to $9.120-$9.320B (from $9.680-$9.960B) and adjusted diluted EPS to $6.15-$6.25 (from $6.85-$7.00), citing a more pressured companion-animal market. Cash fell to $1,476M from $1,941M q/q; long-term debt rose to $9,048M from $5,231M y/y.

drivers.explanation: CEO Peck said a more pressured Companion Animal market — lower clinic visits and pet-owner price sensitivity — reduced demand and heightened competition, prompting targeted commercial investment and pipeline acceleration.

U.S. companion-animal sales fell 11% on softer clinic visits, dermatology/Simparica Trio price sensitivity, and generic competition on Cerenia and Convenia; offset by 23% U.S. livestock growth and 8% international growth led by parasiticides and diagnostics.
Restructuring and certain significant items rose to $77M from $30M y/y and R&D expense grew 4%, outweighing flat revenue and pressuring pretax income despite lower SG&A.
EPS rose 1.2% y/y despite a 4.8% net-income decline because diluted shares outstanding fell 6.2% y/y (445.5M to 417.7M) on continued buybacks, a per-share tailwind.
